The BB(6) work checked partial results for two candidate machines and left both undecided.

The Busy Beaver problem BB(6) asks for the longest possible running time of a halting six-state, two-symbol Turing machine started on a blank tape.

The checked rules describe individual steps or phases of a computation. They do not show what the machines will do forever.

Technical details

Status and exclusions

The source snapshot starts with 663 published representatives and excludes 92, retaining 571 candidates. Exclusions cover published decisions, explicit blank-orbit equivalences, Cryptids and potential Cryptids, existing research claims and work in progress. Blank spreadsheet status alone is not proof that a machine is open.

The later status refresh retained candidates 24 and 444. Equivalence edges for 444 relate blank-start behavior; they do not decide it. Private and unpublished work is outside this status check.

Certified tools and self-checks

The source tools include a fast simulator, an independent reference simulator, translated-cycler and n-gram CPS certificate checkers, a FAR checker, and a symbolic local-proof kernel. The source self-check compared 500 random machines, reproduced known champion runs, and tested both certificate checkers against 1772 known halters with no false positives. Existing small-machine fixtures and corruptions exercise the checkers; they are not new holdout decisions.

These are custom checker certificates. No new decision has been certified with busycoq or Rocq. Third-party simulator implementations are linked from the source instructions rather than vendored here.

Local lemmas and the proof gap

Candidate 24 has 27 checked local lemmas and candidate 444 has 21, giving 48 total. The fresh source verification rejected 198 corrupted variants. Local transition and word-parser statements do not establish global non-halting.

The missing argument is a closed configuration family reachable from blank tape, preserving the left context through carries, delimiter changes and rebuilding, together with the required word induction. Finite simulations and a counter decrement observed in sampled phases do not close this gap.

Final stage 2c outcome

The six-hour investigation finished after 360 min. Candidate 24 remains undecided. The new local certificates contain 118 rules; verification rejected 470 corrupted variants and checked 3973 independent concrete instantiations. These are additional to the earlier 48 lemmas.

The carry and unary-prefix rules do not supply a closed blank-start configuration family through rebuilding. A proposed guarded family contains hypothetical halting starts, so it cannot establish global safety. Those starts are not asserted blank-reachable. A checked finite blank-start anchor also does not prove non-halting.

The final global blank-start search recorded 8 unknown outcomes. Conditional prefix-boundary searches recorded 10 unknown outcomes and 1 external wall cap; retained-context anchor searches recorded 10 unknown outcomes. No target certificate was accepted. The committed decision registry is empty. A decision may be reported only after the full source make verify-decisions accepts a registered certificate.

The three record-search batches found no new records and independently confirmed the saved best known constructions.

The searches tried to improve arrangements of numbers, sets and binary strings that avoid specified conflicts. Independent programs checked the exact conditions; promising attempts with even one remaining conflict were counted as failures.

Technical details

Record-status check

Batch A retained DTS scope 112 and constant-weight code size 36. Batch B retained a covering with 30 blocks and a Schur coloring through 536. These are reproduced published constructions, not new sprint records.

The covering repository web entry could not be fetched. Batch B subsequently checked the maintainer's downloadable metadata and latest archive, which confirm a 30-block construction and lower bound 28. The Schur convention here is the largest colorable integer. A different smallest-uncolorable convention must not be read as an improvement.

Benchmark checker observations

The status review identified boundary tolerances that can admit points outside the intended square or off the unit sphere, producing apparent floating-point gains. Approximate moment tests also do not establish an exact spherical design. These are observations about acceptance rules, not mathematical record improvements, and the sprint did not count them as results.

A separate Schur format mismatch was reproduced. The prompt requests a coloring object, while the benchmark validator accepts a bare list and rejects the wrapper. The published coloring passes in the accepted format and remains independently checked for its mathematical property.

Search effort and negative results

Batch A used CP-SAT, orbit models, neighborhood repair and tabu search. Its committed report discloses a campaign shorter than requested. For example, a code tabu run made 281591612 iterations in 10 min and ended with collision energy 1, an invalid near miss. A DTS run ended at collision energy 2 after 281303682 iterations in 10 min.

Batch B records covering wall time 250 min and Schur wall time 250 min. CP-SAT, SAT neighborhoods, weighted tabu search and restricted orbit/link models found no record. The saved covering near misses leave 3 subsets uncovered; Schur near misses retain 1 violation. Neither is a valid improvement. Timeouts and restricted infeasibility results do not prove the unrestricted problem unsatisfiable.

Final batch C outcome

The W(7,2) search retained a two-colour construction of length 3703 with no monochromatic seven-term arithmetic progression. The binary A(21,10) search retained 42 codewords with minimum distance 10. Both match the published lower bounds; neither is a new record. Colour-first sources write the progression problem as W(2,7). A valid length-3703 colouring proves W > 3703, not the existence of a length-3704 colouring.

The code is a reconstruction in the published quasi-cyclic family with the published parameters. Isomorphism to the original certificate was not proved. The independent verifiers check every progression step or every pairwise distance using exact integers, and derive scores from the constructions.

Credited active wall time was 240 min for progression search and 240 min for code improvement search, excluding interruption gaps. SAT, local search, clique repair and restricted orbit searches found no valid improvement. Saved length-3704 colourings still have 1 progression violation; a code near miss has squared distance-deficit energy 4. These invalid candidates do not establish a new bound.

The source status review links Monroe's van der Waerden bound compilation, Brouwer's binary code table and Kaikkonen's code construction reference. Papers and downloaded source pages are linked, not copied here.
